newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE'S CHAMPIONSHIP CREDENTIALS FACE TOUGH EXAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE'S CHAMPIONSHIP CREDENTIALS FACE TOUGH EXAM.

text.p: Newcastle United's hopes of their first English league title since 1927 face a test of nerve on Sunday when they meet Manchester United, whose last visit to St James' Park turned the course of last season's championship.

Manchester United, who had trailed Newcastle by 12 points six weeks before, cut Newcastle's lead to a single point with a 1-0 win in March and from then on, there was only ever going to be one winner of the title -- and it wasn't going to be Kevin Keegan's side.
Newcastle fans concede that when Eric Cantona's 51st minute strike hit the back of their net they knew in their heart-of-hearts that they would have to wait another season.
Once more Newcastle top the table and United are again posing a serious threat to their hopes, unbeaten in fourth place, just two points behind.

Whether Sunday's match will, in time, be seen as the defining moment in this season's championship chase is still unknown but what is certain is that Newcastle will break down a huge psychological barrier if they beat Manchester United.
Another defeat would not prove as immediately calamitous as the one they suffered last March but it would seriously undermine their confidence.

Manchester manager Alex Ferguson has made little secret that his main target this season is the European Cup and his team's display in their 2-0 champions' league win over Fenerbahce in Turkey showed a great leap forward in terms of maturity and patience they previously lacked in Europe.
United go to Newcastle having won five of their last six games, without a goal conceded in their last five games, and they will give Newcastle their toughest test yet.

Newcastle, with six successive league wins behind them, go into the match buoyed by the form of their 15-million-sterling ($23.8 million) world record signing Alan Shearer, who at one stage during the close-season was linked with Manchester United.

He will line up against them having scored five goals in the last six cup and league matches. With his England strike partner Les Ferdinand having scored nine in his last eight matches, United's rock-solid defence can expect to be severely tested.

While Newcastle look impressive going forwards, their defence has taken a battering recently and if they ultimately fail in their bid for the title, it will be because of the frailties of their backline.

Keegan could well make changes at the back after his team's woeful defensive performance against Fenerbahce in the UEFA Cup on Tuesday which they lost 3-2 and a repeat performance could allow United's young in-form Norwegian striker Ole Gunnar Solskjaer the opportunity to have a field day.
That is unlikely to happen. Despite their rather porous defence, Newcastle look a tougher team to beat now when the pressure is on than they did last season.
A victory over the champions may not clinch the title but it will give Newcastle a serious shot of self-belief, a quality that took a real knock last March.
